1.1.35 — Lighter and smoother

  • Much less memory. Only your current tab and the one before it stay ready. Others sleep, and they sleep sooner, so a handful of busy sites takes about half the memory it did.
  • Tabs wake where you left them. A sleeping tab comes back at the same spot with its Back history, showing a picture of the page until it's ready.
  • Gives memory back. When your Mac runs short, tabs out of view go to sleep right away. Tabs playing video or in a call stay awake.
  • Quiet when idle. The New Tab page no longer works in the background, so Pane uses almost no power when you're not using it.
  • A smoother sidebar. The page keeps its size while the sidebar slides, so the slide stutters far less.

1.1.34 — Video, done properly

  • Picture in picture that works. Float any video with the button by the address, or ⌃⌘P, and it stays with you. Leave a playing tab and it floats on its own; come back and it lands in the page.
  • Full screen that works. Sites' own full screen buttons now do what they say, and ⌥⌘F takes the page's video full screen from anywhere.
  • Video controls. Site settings has picture in picture, full screen and playback speed when a page has a video. Embedded players count too.
  • A bar above the page. With the address on top, the bar takes the site's color and the site starts below it, so nothing is covered. It slides up as you scroll down.
  • The address bar opens in place. Click it and that same bar expands, with no second one appearing.
  • A new swipe. Two fingers sideways bring in a glass circle with an arrow that follows you until it's ready to go back or forward.
  • New tab means the New Tab page. Add Tab opens the page, not a pop-out.
  • Dark glass What's New. This window, in dark Liquid Glass.

1.1.33 — Just the site

  • Nothing above the page. Sites run right to the top, with the glass controls floating over them, whether the sidebar is open or closed. The coloured bar is gone.
  • Address in the sidebar, if you like. Settings › Appearance › Address and controls puts back, forward, reload and the address at the top of the sidebar instead.
  • A real slide. The sidebar and your tabs slide out to the left together as the page grows, with no fading.
  • Frosted messages. The little messages at the bottom of the page are frosted Liquid Glass.
  • A simpler sidebar. The space's name is gone from above your tabs. To rename a space or change its icon and color, use the pencil next to it in the bottom-left menu.
  • The new logo everywhere. What's New, Settings and your member card all show it now.
